chapters.title: AI to the rescue: a new visualization engine
Building your first AI chart module

takeaways: The native Power Apps chart control is rigid by design: rendering, colors, scaling and fonts are sealed in templates, so styling and dynamic behavior require brittle workarounds.
An AI prompt can receive a trimmed JSON payload from Power Apps, generate chart code with code interpreter and return a Base64 image that an HTML text control displays.
Filter and flatten data in Power Apps before sending it, write precise prompts with colors, fonts and dimensions, and treat 3D charts as experimental prototypes.
hook: Native Power Apps charts look dated and resist styling, so makers end up exporting data to Power BI or pasting screenshots. This episode shows Power Apps makers how to let an AI prompt with code interpreter render modern, filter-aware charts as images inside their apps, and what to watch for with JSON payloads and prompts.
